framework: Foundry (forge) inside a yarn-managed Balancer V3 monorepo fork (per-pkg foundry.toml)

build.compile: forge compile (from pkg/pool-quantamm, pkg/pool-hooks, or pkg/interfaces)
build.notes: ffi=true is set in pkg/pool-quantamm/foundry.toml; build depends on node_modules (Balancer @balancer-labs, @openzeppelin, @prb/math PRBMath, permit2, @chainlink, forge-std) resolved via yarn workspaces.

dependencies: @balancer-labs/v3-* (vault, solidity-utils, interfaces — Balancer V3 base infrastructure)
out_of_scope: All base Balancer V3 infrastructure (pkg/vault, pkg/pool-weighted, pkg/pool-stable, pkg/pool-gyro, pkg/pool-utils, pkg/solidity-utils) except where an issue is a combination of batch-swap router + QuantAMMWeightedPool
Vault / Swap / deposit / withdraw mechanics inherited from Balancer V3
Issues already acknowledged in included root + pool-quantamm audit folder reports (known issues)

compatibilities.tokens: Standard ERC20 only. Non-standard (rebasing, allowlist, fee-on-transfer/double-entrypoint, etc.) explicitly OUT of scope.

known_issues_out_of_scope: Oracle manipulation of update-rule weight trajectories or fee quantity (Chainlink assumed in-spec); but in-spec-data mishandling (e.g. wrong decimal conversion in Chainlink wrapper) IS in scope

Unguarded theoretical rule-equation limits that revert (div-by-0, caught overflow) are expected to revert; BUT silent overflows, unintended sign changes vs whitepaper, weight vectors violating whitepaper equations, or guard-rail breaches inside the weighted pool ARE in scope
Multi-block MEV when guard rails are configured inappropriately (inappropriate-guard-rail config is out of scope)
Random/irregular update-interval effects; failures/restarts of updates; block.timestamp use
Manipulation on 0-fee pools; single-asset-deposit extreme-value failures (unless usable to attack the pool without out-of-scope properties)
quantammAdmin assumed a correctly configured OZ timelock and secure; malicious-admin-takeover issues out of scope
Pool-creator trust levels: types 1 and 2 trust the pool creator; TYPE 3 (creator NOT in approvedPoolActions) is untrusted and creator manipulation IS in scope
ambiguities: README references included root + pool-quantamm 'audit folder' reports as the source of known/acknowledged issues; those acknowledged items are out of scope but the exact list lives in audits/ folder reports, not the README.

Interfaces and QuantammBasedRuleHelpers are listed in scope but are largely declarative; substantive logic concentrates in UpdateWeightRunner, QuantAMMWeightedPool, the rules, the rules/base estimators, QuantAMMStorage, the oracles, and UpliftOnlyExample/LPNFT.
